417:## Epic 2: Biometric Authentication Vault
418-
419-Users unlock the app with Face ID/Touch ID (or PIN fallback) before any personal data is ever shown, with no lockout path and no biometric data ever leaving the device.
420-
421-### Story 2.1: Biometric/PIN App-Access Gate
422-
423-As a user,
424-I want the app to require Face ID, Touch ID, or PIN before showing any of my data,
425-So that my journal stays private even if someone else picks up my phone.
426-
427-**Acceptance Criteria:**
428-
429-**Given** the app is cold-started or resumed after the idle timeout
430-**When** the vault gate evaluates
431-**Then** no screen other than the vault/login screen is reachable until authentication succeeds.
432-
433-**Given** the `go_router` redirect
434-**When** it evaluates on any navigation attempt
435-**Then** it composes exactly two gates in fixed order — `VaultStatus` first, then `SessionStatus` (AD-14) — and neither gate ever makes a network call to validate itself; biometric validation is 100% on-device, so no biometric data or call ever reaches the backend.
436-
437-**Given** Face ID/Touch ID is available and enabled
438-**When** I open the app
439-**Then** the OS biometric prompt appears and, on success, routes me straight to Home/Chat.
440-**And** `features/vault/domain` exposes a `VaultStatus` stream the same way `features/auth/domain` exposes `SessionStatus` (AD-8 pattern), registered once in DI.
441-
442-### Story 2.2: Biometric-Failure Fallback to PIN
443-
444-As a user whose biometric check fails,
445-I want to fall back to entering a PIN,
446-So that I'm never locked out of my own journal.
447-
448-**Acceptance Criteria:**
449-
450-**Given** Face ID/Touch ID fails to recognize me
451-**When** the failure is reported
452-**Then** "Não foi possível reconhecer — digite seu PIN" appears with a PIN entry path always reachable — never a dead end.
453-
454-**Given** repeated biometric failures trigger an OS-level lockout
455-**When** that lockout is detected
456-**Then** the app routes to its own PIN fallback rather than retrying against the OS.

# Compile Epic Context

**Task**
Given an epic number, the epics file, the planning artifacts directory, and a desired output path, compile a clean, focused, developer-ready context file (`epic-<N>-context.md`).

**Steps**

1. Read the epics file and extract the target epic's title, goal, and list of stories.
2. Scan the planning artifacts directory for the standard files (PRD, architecture, UX/design, product brief).
3. Pull only the information relevant to this epic.
4. Write the compiled context to the exact output path using the format below.

## Exact Output Format

Use these headings:

```markdown
# Epic {N} Context: {Epic Title}

<!-- Compiled from planning artifacts. Edit freely. Regenerate with compile-epic-context if planning docs change. -->

## Goal

{One clear paragraph: what this epic achieves and why it matters.}

## Stories

- Story X.Y: Brief title only
- ...

## Requirements & Constraints

{Relevant functional/non-functional requirements and success criteria for this epic (describe by purpose, not source).}

## Technical Decisions

{Key architecture decisions, constraints, patterns, data models, and conventions relevant to this epic.}

## UX & Interaction Patterns

{Relevant UX flows, interaction patterns, and design constraints (omit section entirely if nothing relevant).}

## Cross-Story Dependencies

{Dependencies between stories in this epic or with other epics/systems (omit if none).}
```

## Rules

- **Scope aggressively.** Include only what a developer working on any story in this epic actually needs. When in doubt, leave it out — the developer can always read the full planning doc.
- **Describe by purpose, not by source.** Write "API responses must include pagination metadata" not "Per PRD section 3.2.1, pagination is required." Planning doc internals will change; the constraint won't.
- **No full copies.** Never quote source documents, section numbers, or paste large blocks verbatim. Always distill.
- **No story-level details.** The story list is for orientation only. Individual story specs handle the details.
- **Nothing derivable from the codebase.** Don't document what a developer can learn by reading the code.
- **Be concise and actionable.** Target 800–1500 tokens total. This file loads into build's context alongside other material.
- **Never hallucinate content.** If source material doesn't say something, don't invent it.
- **Omit empty sections entirely**, except Goal and Stories, which are always required.

## Error handling

- **If the epics file is missing or the target epic is not found:** write nothing and report the problem to the calling agent. Goal and Stories cannot be populated without a usable epics file.
- **If planning artifacts are missing or empty:** still produce the file with Goal and Stories populated from the epics file, and note the gap in the Goal section. Never hallucinate content to fill missing sections.

# Epic 2 Context: Biometric Authentication Vault

<!-- Compiled from planning artifacts. Edit freely. Regenerate with compile-epic-context if planning docs change. -->

## Goal

Put a device-validated access barrier in front of every screen that shows user data: Face ID or Touch ID with a PIN fallback, cold-start and after a fixed idle timeout, with zero lockout path and zero biometric data or call ever reaching the backend. This closes the one entry point into the app that Epic 1 left as a placeholder, and every later feature's data is only ever reachable once this gate has passed.

## Stories

- Story 2.1: Biometric/PIN App-Access Gate
- Story 2.2: Biometric-Failure Fallback to PIN
- Story 2.3: Fixed 5-Minute Idle Re-Authentication Timeout
- Story 2.4: Biometric Preference Persistence

## Requirements & Constraints

- No screen other than the vault/login screen is reachable before authentication succeeds, on cold start and after the idle timeout.
- Biometric validation is 100% on-device; no biometric data or biometric call ever reaches the backend. `AuthInvalid` can only ever originate from password login — never from a local vault/PIN check, so no vault failure is ever mapped to that Failure subtype.
- A failed biometric attempt always offers a PIN entry path — never a dead end, never a lockout. An OS-level lockout from repeated biometric failures is detected and routed to the app's own PIN fallback, not retried against the OS.
- The idle re-authentication timeout is exactly 5 minutes, fixed and not user-configurable: resuming before 5 minutes prompts nothing; resuming at or after 5 minutes always prompts re-authentication, regardless of any user setting.
- The biometric on/off preference is persisted server-side via `PATCH /account/settings` (surfacing the standard Failure contract on error), not cached only on-device — it is re-fetched from the account on every app load, including after reinstall. Disabling biometrics still leaves PIN as the access method; the vault itself can never be fully turned off.
- Performance floor applies as elsewhere: local UI interactions <100ms; any network call >300ms shows a loading indicator.

## Technical Decisions

- New module `features/vault/` owns this epic. It exposes a `VaultStatus` stream from `features/vault/domain`, mirroring how `features/auth/domain` exposes `SessionStatus` — registered once in DI as a singleton, same pattern, no second instance.
- The single `go_router` top-level redirect (already scaffolded by Epic 1/F000 for `SessionStatus`) is extended, not rebuilt: it composes exactly two gates in fixed order — `VaultStatus` first, then `SessionStatus` — because the vault gates whether anything may be shown at all, before any network/session state is considered. Neither gate ever makes a network call to validate itself.
- Biometrics via `local_auth` (^3.0.2); any local secret (e.g. PIN) via `flutter_secure_storage` (^11.2.0). `NSFaceIDUsageDescription` is required in `Info.plist` for Face ID (not for Touch ID). `local_auth`'s `biometryLockout`/`lockedOut` error has no programmatic reset — catch it and fall through to the app's own PIN path. `stickyAuth` behavior is relevant to resuming an in-flight check when the app returns to foreground.
- The 5-minute idle timeout is app logic (lifecycle observation on backgrounding/resuming), not plugin-provided, and must be implemented as a fixed parameter living inside `features/vault/domain` — explicitly not a shared `core/` constant — and is never re-tuned by any later story.
- The biometric preference toggle itself is persisted through `PATCH /account/settings`, which belongs to `features/account/` (not `features/vault/`) — story 2.4 is the point where a minimal Configurações screen is introduced (replacing Epic 1's placeholder) containing only this toggle; Epic 8 later extends the same screen with profile editing, dashboard, and account actions, so it is never recreated from scratch.
- Standard project-wide rules apply: domain layer imports neither `package:flutter` nor `data/`; repositories return `Either<Failure, T>`; no hardcoded visual values outside `design_tokens.dart`.

## UX & Interaction Patterns

- PIN keypad: numeric 3×4 grid + backspace, progress dots above, rendered entirely in the structural palette (no accent color on digits).
- PIN entry auto-advances 350ms after the 4th digit is entered — no explicit "confirm" tap.
- Biometric-failure copy: "Não foi possível reconhecer — digite seu PIN."
- Screen-reader labels must announce the failure transition (state changes, not just static state).
- The PIN keypad is one of the tightest-fit surfaces for Dynamic Type — digits must not truncate at the largest accessibility text size.
- Tap targets ≥44pt.

## Cross-Story Dependencies

- Depends on Epic 1/F000: the `go_router` redirect skeleton and the `SessionStatus` stream already exist (stories 1.5/1.6). This epic plugs the `VaultStatus` half into that same redirect rather than building a second, competing gate.
- Story 2.4 depends on `features/account/`'s `PATCH /account/settings` and introduces the Configurações screen shell that Epic 8 later extends — that screen must not be rebuilt from scratch in Epic 8.
- Within the epic, 2.1 (the gate itself) must exist before 2.2 (its failure fallback) and 2.3 (its timeout trigger) make sense; 2.4's persisted preference governs whether 2.1's gate is biometric-first or PIN-only, so it reads that preference at startup regardless of build order.

Give me a concise report with file:line references for each of the 9 points above. Do not read every file exhaustively — target the specific ones named. Keep the report focused and under 2500 words.

1	import 'package:freezed_annotation/freezed_annotation.dart';
2	
3	part 'failure.freezed.dart';
4	
5	/// AD-3 — the one closed `Failure` hierarchy, exactly 14 subtypes: the 13
6	/// codes from `docs/input/backend/error-taxonomy.md` plus the local-only
7	/// `malformedResponse` (client-side parse failure, never sent by the
8	/// backend). Never redefined or subset per feature; every repository method
9	/// returns `Either<Failure, T>` built from this type (RNF09).
10	///
11	/// `retryable` is derived here, once, from the 6 server `retryable:true`
12	/// codes (AD-4) — no other file re-decides which codes retry.
13	@freezed
14	sealed class Failure with _$Failure {
15	  const factory Failure.authExpired({required String message}) = AuthExpired;
16	  const factory Failure.authInvalid({required String message}) = AuthInvalid;
17	  const factory Failure.networkTimeout({required String message}) =
18	      NetworkTimeout;
19	  const factory Failure.networkOffline({required String message}) =
20	      NetworkOffline;
21	  const factory Failure.validation({required String message}) = Validation;
22	  const factory Failure.piiCheckFailed({required String message}) =
23	      PiiCheckFailed;
24	  const factory Failure.embeddingFailed({required String message}) =
25	      EmbeddingFailed;
26	  const factory Failure.aiGenerationTimeout({required String message}) =
27	      AiGenerationTimeout;
28	  const factory Failure.notFound({required String message}) = NotFound;
29	  const factory Failure.rateLimited({required String message}) = RateLimited;
30	  const factory Failure.exportEmptyPeriod({required String message}) =
31	      ExportEmptyPeriod;
32	  const factory Failure.payloadTooLarge({required String message}) =
33	      PayloadTooLarge;
34	  const factory Failure.ocrNoText({required String message}) = OcrNoText;
35	
36	  /// Local-only — the client's own parse-failure detection. `retryable` is
37	  /// hardcoded `false` for this subtype (AD-3).
38	  const factory Failure.malformedResponse({required String message}) =
39	      MalformedResponse;
40	
41	  const Failure._();
42	
43	  /// The 6 server `retryable:true` codes (AD-4). Every other code —
44	  /// including the local `malformedResponse` — is `false`.
45	  bool get retryable => switch (this) {
46	        NetworkTimeout() => true,
47	        NetworkOffline() => true,
48	        PiiCheckFailed() => true,
49	        EmbeddingFailed() => true,
50	        AiGenerationTimeout() => true,
51	        RateLimited() => true,
52	        AuthExpired() ||
53	        AuthInvalid() ||
54	        Validation() ||
55	        NotFound() ||
56	        ExportEmptyPeriod() ||
57	        PayloadTooLarge() ||
58	        OcrNoText() ||
59	        MalformedResponse() =>
60	          false,
61	      };
62	
63	  /// Maps a backend error `code` (`error-taxonomy.md`) to its `Failure`
64	  /// subtype. An unrecognized code (should never happen — the taxonomy is
65	  /// closed) falls back to [Failure.malformedResponse] rather than throwing,
66	  /// so no repository ever lets an unmapped error escape (RNF09).
67	  factory Failure.fromCode(String code, String message) => switch (code) {
68	        'AUTH_EXPIRED' => Failure.authExpired(message: message),
69	        'AUTH_INVALID' => Failure.authInvalid(message: message),
70	        'NETWORK_TIMEOUT' => Failure.networkTimeout(message: message),
71	        'NETWORK_OFFLINE' => Failure.networkOffline(message: message),
72	        'VALIDATION_ERROR' => Failure.validation(message: message),
73	        'PII_CHECK_FAILED' => Failure.piiCheckFailed(message: message),
74	        'EMBEDDING_FAILED' => Failure.embeddingFailed(message: message),
75	        'AI_GENERATION_TIMEOUT' =>
76	          Failure.aiGenerationTimeout(message: message),
77	        'NOT_FOUND' => Failure.notFound(message: message),
78	        'RATE_LIMITED' => Failure.rateLimited(message: message),
79	        'EXPORT_EMPTY_PERIOD' => Failure.exportEmptyPeriod(message: message),
80	        'PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE' => Failure.payloadTooLarge(message: message),
81	        'OCR_NO_TEXT' => Failure.ocrNoText(message: message),
82	        _ => Failure.malformedResponse(message: message),
83	      };
84	}

18	/// A Flutter plugin for authenticating the user identity locally.
19	class LocalAuthentication {
20	  /// Authenticates the user with biometrics available on the device while also
21	  /// allowing the user to use device authentication - pin, pattern, passcode.
22	  ///
23	  /// Returns true if the user successfully authenticated.
24	  ///
25	  /// If the user fails the authentication challenge without any side effects,
26	  /// returns false. For other other failures cases, throws a
27	  /// [LocalAuthException] with details about the reason it did not succeed.
28	  ///
29	  /// [localizedReason] is the message to show to user while prompting them
30	  /// for authentication. This is typically along the lines of: 'Authenticate
31	  /// to access MyApp.'. This must not be empty.
32	  ///
33	  /// Provide [authMessages] if you want to customize messages in the dialogs.
34	  ///
35	  /// Set [biometricOnly] to true to prevent authentications from using
36	  /// non-biometric local authentication such as pin, passcode, or pattern.
37	  ///
38	  /// [sensitiveTransaction], which defaults to true, controls whether
39	  /// platform-specific precautions are enabled, such as showing a confirmation
40	  /// dialog after face unlock is recognized to make sure the user meant to
41	  /// unlock their device.
42	  ///
43	  /// On mobile platforms, authentication may be stopped by the system when the
44	  /// app is backgrounded during an authentication. Set
45	  /// [persistAcrossBackgrounding] to true to have the plugin automatically
46	  /// retry the authentication on foregrounding instead of failing with an error
47	  /// on backgrounding.
48	  Future<bool> authenticate({
49	    required String localizedReason,
50	    Iterable<AuthMessages> authMessages = const <AuthMessages>[
51	      IOSAuthMessages(),
52	      AndroidAuthMessages(),
53	      WindowsAuthMessages(),
54	    ],
55	    bool biometricOnly = false,
56	    bool sensitiveTransaction = true,
57	    bool persistAcrossBackgrounding = false,
58	  }) {
59	    return LocalAuthPlatform.instance.authenticate(
60	      localizedReason: localizedReason,
61	      authMessages: authMessages,
62	      options: AuthenticationOptions(
63	        stickyAuth: persistAcrossBackgrounding,
64	        biometricOnly: biometricOnly,
65	        sensitiveTransaction: sensitiveTransaction,
66	        // This is a legacy option; implementations compatible with 3.x plus
67	        // should always assume this is false, so set it accordingly.
68	        useErrorDialogs: false,
69	      ),
70	    );
71	  }
72	
73	  /// Cancels any in-progress authentication, returning true if auth was
74	  /// canceled successfully.
75	  ///
76	  /// This API may not be supported by all platforms.
77	  ///
78	  /// Returns false if there was some error, no authentication is in progress,
79	  /// or the current platform lacks support.
80	  Future<bool> stopAuthentication() async {
81	    return LocalAuthPlatform.instance.stopAuthentication();
82	  }
83	
84	  /// Returns true if device is capable of checking biometrics.
85	  Future<bool> get canCheckBiometrics => LocalAuthPlatform.instance.deviceSupportsBiometrics();
86	
87	  /// Returns true if device is capable of checking biometrics or is able to
88	  /// fail over to device credentials.
89	  Future<bool> isDeviceSupported() async => LocalAuthPlatform.instance.isDeviceSupported();
90	
91	  /// Returns a list of the biometrics that the app can currently use for
92	  /// authentication.
93	  ///
94	  /// Note that this may not include all biometrics enrolled on the device.
95	  /// For example, on iOS, biometrics may be enrolled on the device but
96	  /// remain unavailable to the app if the user has not granted the required
97	  /// permissions to use them.
98	  Future<List<BiometricType>> getAvailableBiometrics() =>
99	      LocalAuthPlatform.instance.getEnrolledBiometrics();
100	}

7	/// An exception thrown by the plugin when there is authentication failure, or
8	/// some other error.
9	@immutable
10	class LocalAuthException implements Exception {
11	  /// Creates a new exception with the given information.
12	  const LocalAuthException({
13	    required this.code,
14	    this.description,
15	    this.details,
16	  });
17	
18	  /// The type of failure.
19	  final LocalAuthExceptionCode code;
20	
21	  /// A human-readable description of the failure.
22	  final String? description;
23	
24	  /// Any additional details about the failure.
25	  final Object? details;
26	
27	  @override
28	  String toString() =>
29	      '${objectRuntimeType(this, 'LocalAuthException')}(code ${code.name}, $description, $details)';
30	}
31	
32	/// Types of [LocalAuthException]s, as indicated by [LocalAuthException.code].
33	///
34	/// Adding new values to this enum in the future will *not* be considered a
35	/// breaking change, so clients should not assume they can exhaustively match
36	/// exception codes. Clients should always include a default or other fallback.
37	enum LocalAuthExceptionCode {
38	  /// An authentication operation is already in progress, and has not completed.
39	  ///
40	  /// A new authentication cannot be started while the Future for a previous
41	  /// authentication is still outstanding.
42	  authInProgress,
43	
44	  /// UI needs to be displayed, but could not be.
45	  ///
46	  /// For example, this can be returned on Android if a call tries to show UI
47	  /// when no Activity is available.
48	  uiUnavailable,
49	
50	  /// The operation was canceled by the user.
51	  userCanceled,
52	
53	  /// The operation was canceled due to a device-specific timeout.
54	  timeout,
55	
56	  /// The operation was canceled by a system event.
57	  ///
58	  /// For example, on mobile this may be returned if the application is
59	  /// backgrounded during authentication.
60	  systemCanceled,
61	
62	  /// The device has no credentials configured.
63	  ///
64	  /// For example, on mobile this would be returned if the device has no
65	  /// enrolled biometrics and no fallback authentication mechanism set such as
66	  /// a passcode, pin, or pattern.
67	  noCredentialsSet,
68	
69	  /// The device is capable of biometric authentication, but no biometrics are
70	  /// enrolled.
71	  noBiometricsEnrolled,
72	
73	  /// The device does not have biometric hardware.
74	  noBiometricHardware,
75	
76	  /// The device has, or can have, biometric hardware, but none is currently
77	  /// available.
78	  ///
79	  /// Examples include:
80	  /// - Hardware that is currently in use by another application.
81	  /// - Devices that have previously paired with bluetooth biometric hardware,
82	  ///   but are not currently paired to it.
83	  ///
84	  /// Devices that could have removable hardware attached may return either this
85	  /// or [noBiometricHardware] depending on the platform implementation.
86	  /// Platforms should generally only return this code if the system provides
87	  /// information indicating that the device has previously had such hardware.
88	  biometricHardwareTemporarilyUnavailable,
89	
90	  /// Authentication has temporarily been locked out, and should be re-attempted
91	  /// later.
92	  ///
93	  /// For example, devices may return this error after too many failed
94	  /// authentication attempts.
95	  temporaryLockout,
96	
97	  /// Biometric authentication has been locked until some other authentication
98	  /// has succeeded.
99	  ///
100	  /// Applications that do not require biometric authentication should generally
101	  /// handle this error by re-attempting authentication with fallback to
102	  /// non-biometrics allowed. Applications that require biometrics should
103	  /// prompt users to resolve the lockout.
104	  biometricLockout,
105	
106	  /// The user indicated via system-provided UI that they want to use a fallback
107	  /// authentication option instead of biometrics.
108	  ///
109	  /// Whether this can be returned depends on the platform implementation and
110	  /// the authentication configuration options. Applications should generally
111	  /// handle this error by offering the user an alternate authentication option.
112	  userRequestedFallback,
113	
114	  /// The authentication attempt failed due to some device-level error.
115	  ///
116	  /// The [LocalAuthException.description] should contain more details about the
117	  /// error.
118	  deviceError,
119	
120	  /// The authentication attempt failed due to some unknown or unexpected error.
121	  ///
122	  /// The [LocalAuthException.description] should contain more details about the
123	  /// error.
124	  unknownError,
125	}

---
title: 'Biometric/PIN App-Access Gate'
type: 'feature'
created: '2026-11-03'
status: 'draft'
review_loop_iteration: 0
context: []
---

<frozen-after-approval reason="human-owned intent — do not modify unless human renegotiates">

## Intent

**Problem:** Epic 1 left every screen reachable with no device-level access barrier; Epic 2 requires Face ID/Touch ID (PIN fallback is Story 2.2) to block all screens except the vault/login screen, on cold start, before any data is shown.

**Approach:** Add a `features/vault/` module exposing a `VaultStatus` stream that mirrors `features/auth/domain`'s `SessionStatus` pattern exactly, and extend the single existing `go_router` redirect so it composes `VaultStatus` first, then `SessionStatus` (the seam is already commented in-place). A new `/vault` route shows a minimal lock screen that auto-triggers the OS biometric prompt via `local_auth` and offers a manual retry on failure — no PIN entry UI (that's Story 2.2).

## Boundaries & Constraints

**Always:** `_redirect` checks `VaultStatus` before `SessionStatus`, never a second `GoRouter`/`redirect`. Vault makes zero network calls; `authenticate()` never produces `Failure.authInvalid` (reserved for password login). `local_auth.authenticate()` is called with `biometricOnly: true` so it never silently falls back to the OS's own device passcode screen. `VaultStatus` starts `locked` at construction (not nullable — no async warm-up needed) and only a successful `authenticate()` flips it to `unlocked`.

**Ask First:** None — remaining technical choices (lock-screen copy, retry-button wording) are decided per AGENTS.md's "decide and proceed."

**Never:** No PIN entry screen, no idle-timeout re-lock, no biometric-preference persistence — Stories 2.2/2.3/2.4. Never set `biometricOnly: false` (would let the OS's own passcode bypass Cerne's intended PIN flow).

## I/O & Edge-Case Matrix

| Scenario | Input / State | Expected Output / Behavior | Error Handling |
|----------|--------------|---------------------------|----------------|
| Cold start, biometrics succeed | `VaultStatus.locked`, app opened, OS prompt confirms | `authenticate()` emits `unlocked`; redirect falls through to existing `SessionStatus` logic (Home if authenticated) | N/A |
| Cold start, biometrics fail/cancelled/unavailable | `authenticate()` returns `false` or throws `LocalAuthException` | Status stays `locked`; lock screen shows retry button | `Left(Failure.malformedResponse(...))`, no crash |
| Any navigation while locked | `location != /vault`, `VaultStatus.locked` | redirect returns `/vault` | N/A |

</frozen-after-approval>

## Code Map

- `lib/features/auth/domain/entities/session_status.dart`, `.../repositories/session_repository.dart`, `data/repositories/session_repository_impl.dart` — exact pattern to mirror (`Stream.multi` replay-to-late-listeners, `_emit`/`isClosed` guard, `dispose:` wiring).
- `lib/core/navigation/app_router.dart:17-25` (`AppRoutePaths`), `:38-81` (`buildAppRouter`), `:94-98` (seam comment already marks this exact change), `:99-123` (`_redirect`), `:129-148` (`_GoRouterRefreshStream`, currently wraps one stream).
- `lib/main.dart:48,63-67` — `_sessionRepository = sl<SessionRepository>()` call site to mirror for vault.
- `lib/core/di/injection_container.dart:79` — `registerAuthFeature()` call site; add `registerVaultFeature()` after it.
- `lib/features/auth/auth_injection.dart` — DI registration pattern (`registerLazySingleton` + `dispose:`) to mirror.
- `lib/core/failure/failure.dart:38-39` — `Failure.malformedResponse` is the only local-failure subtype to use here.
- `pubspec.yaml:49-50` — `local_auth: ^3.0.2`, `flutter_secure_storage: ^11.2.0` already present, no change.
- `~/.pub-cache/.../local_auth-3.0.2/lib/src/local_auth.dart` — current API: `authenticate()` returns `Future<bool>`, throws `LocalAuthException` (not `PlatformException`) on error.
- `ios/Runner/Info.plist` — `NSFaceIDUsageDescription` absent, must be added.
- `test/core/navigation/app_router_test.dart` — every existing case constructs `buildAppRouter(sessionRepository: ..., ...)` directly; each call site needs a second fake `VaultRepository` (default `unlocked`) added.
- `test/main_test.dart:89-97` — `setUp` calls real `setupCoreDependencies()`; since `CerneApp` will now also resolve `sl<VaultRepository>()`, swap in a fake pre-`unlocked` one here so existing auth/session cases are unaffected.

## Tasks & Acceptance

**Execution:**
- [ ] `lib/features/vault/domain/entities/vault_status.dart` -- create `enum VaultStatus { locked, unlocked }` -- mirrors `SessionStatus`.
- [ ] `lib/features/vault/domain/repositories/vault_repository.dart` -- create `abstract class VaultRepository` (`statusStream`, non-null `currentStatus` defaulting `locked`, `authenticate()`, `dispose()`) -- mirrors `SessionRepository` (RNF09: `Either<Failure, Unit>`).
- [ ] `lib/features/vault/data/repositories/vault_repository_impl.dart` -- create `VaultRepositoryImpl(LocalAuthentication)`; `authenticate()` calls `.authenticate(localizedReason: ..., biometricOnly: true, persistAcrossBackgrounding: true)`; success emits `unlocked`+`right(unit)`; `false`/`LocalAuthException` -> `left(Failure.malformedResponse(...))`, status unchanged -- zero network, never `authInvalid`.
- [ ] `lib/features/vault/vault_injection.dart` -- create `registerVaultFeature()` -- mirrors `auth_injection.dart`.
- [ ] `lib/core/di/injection_container.dart` -- call `registerVaultFeature()` after `registerAuthFeature()`.
- [ ] `lib/core/navigation/app_router.dart` -- add `vaultLock` path; thread `vaultRepository` through `buildAppRouter`/`_redirect`; new top branch returns `vaultLock` whenever status isn't `unlocked`; extend the existing authenticated/expired `location == boot || auth` check to also include `vaultLock`; extend `_GoRouterRefreshStream` to subscribe to both streams -- composes the two gates in fixed order (AD-14).
- [ ] `lib/features/vault/presentation/screens/vault_lock_screen.dart` -- `StatefulWidget` calling `vaultRepository.authenticate()` once in `initState`, with a "Tentar novamente" retry button on failure -- no PIN UI; `DesignTokens` only.
- [ ] `lib/main.dart` -- resolve `sl<VaultRepository>()`, pass into `buildAppRouter`.
- [ ] `ios/Runner/Info.plist` -- add `NSFaceIDUsageDescription`.
- [ ] `test/features/vault/data/repositories/vault_repository_impl_test.dart` -- unit-test the I/O matrix with a mocked `LocalAuthentication`.
- [ ] `test/core/navigation/app_router_test.dart` -- add a fake `VaultRepository` (default `unlocked`) to every existing call site; add cases: locked overrides any `SessionStatus`; unlocked + authenticated at `/vault` routes home.
- [ ] `test/main_test.dart` -- swap in a fake pre-unlocked `VaultRepository` in `setUp`; add one new test: cold start stays on `/vault` until a fake `authenticate()` success routes to Home.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- Given the app is cold-started, when the vault gate evaluates, then no screen other than `/vault` is reachable until `authenticate()` succeeds.
- Given the redirect evaluates on any navigation attempt, then it composes exactly two gates in fixed order (`VaultStatus` then `SessionStatus`) and neither ever makes a network call.
- Given Face ID/Touch ID is available and the user opens the app, when the OS prompt succeeds, then the app routes to Home/Chat via the existing session logic, and `features/vault/domain` exposes `VaultStatus` registered once in DI.

## Design Notes

`biometricOnly: true` is the one easy-to-miss detail: `local_auth`'s default (`false`) lets the OS's own device-passcode UI satisfy `authenticate()`, which would bypass Cerne's own PIN screen (Story 2.2) entirely — `true` forces biometrics-or-fail, matching the epic's intent that PIN is Cerne's own screen, never iOS's/Android's.

`VaultStatus.currentStatus` is deliberately non-nullable (unlike `SessionStatus?`) — the vault's "locked" state is known synchronously at construction, with no async restore step, so there's no boot-loading gap to represent with `null`.

## Verification

**Commands:**
- `fvm flutter analyze` -- expected: zero issues.
- `fvm flutter test` -- expected: all pass, including new vault tests.

**Manual checks (if no CLI):**
- No device/simulator exists yet (AGENTS.md) — the real OS biometric prompt itself is unverifiable until one does; this is a known, pre-existing gap, not introduced by this story.

# Sync Sprint Status

Shared sub-step for updating `sprint-status.yaml` during build. Called from any route (plan-code-review, one-shot, future routes) with a `target_status` parameter.

## Preconditions

Skip this entire file (return to caller) if ANY of:
- `story_key` is unset
- `/Users/wagnerduarte/Documents/Faculdade/2026.2/TCC/cerne-ciclo-b/_bmad-output/implementation-artifacts/sprint-status.yaml` does not exist on disk

## Instructions

1. Load the FULL `/Users/wagnerduarte/Documents/Faculdade/2026.2/TCC/cerne-ciclo-b/_bmad-output/implementation-artifacts/sprint-status.yaml` file.
2. Find the `development_status` entry matching `{story_key}`. If not found, warn the user once (`"{story_key} not found in sprint-status; skipping sprint sync"`) and return to caller.
3. **Idempotency check.** If `development_status[{story_key}]` is already at `target_status` or a later state (`review` is later than `in-progress`; `done` is later than both), return to caller — no write needed. Never regress a story's status.
4. Set `development_status[{story_key}]` to `{target_status}`.
5. **Epic lift (only when `target_status` = `in-progress`).** Derive the parent epic key as `epic-{N}` from the leading numeric segment of `{story_key}` (e.g., `3-2-digest-delivery` → `epic-3`). If that entry exists and is `backlog`, set it to `in-progress`. Leave it alone otherwise. Skip this sub-step entirely when `target_status` is not `in-progress`.
6. Refresh `last_updated` to the current date.
7. Save the file, preserving ALL comments and structure including STATUS DEFINITIONS and WORKFLOW NOTES.

Success → emits `unlocked` + `Right(unit)`. `false` or caught `LocalAuthException` → `Left(Failure.malformedResponse(...))`, status stays `locked`, never `Failure.authInvalid`. Zero network calls anywhere. `Stream.multi` replay pattern mirrors `SessionRepositoryImpl` exactly, with an `isClosed` guard in `_emit`.
  - `lib/features/vault/vault_injection.dart` — `registerVaultFeature()` registers `LocalAuthentication` + `VaultRepository` as lazy singletons, `dispose:` wired to `sl.reset()`.
  - `lib/features/vault/presentation/screens/vault_lock_screen.dart` — `VaultLockScreen` (StatefulWidget), auto-calls `authenticate()` once in `initState`, shows an `AppButton` "Tentar novamente" retry on failure, never navigates imperatively (the router's `refreshListenable` handles that once `currentStatus` flips). `DesignTokens`-only styling.
  - `test/features/vault/data/repositories/vault_repository_impl_test.dart` — full I/O matrix with a mocked `LocalAuthentication`.
  
  **Modified files**
  - `lib/core/di/injection_container.dart` — calls `registerVaultFeature()` after `registerAuthFeature()`.
  - `lib/core/navigation/app_router.dart` — added `AppRoutePaths.vaultLock = '/vault'`; `buildAppRouter` now requires `vaultRepository`; `_redirect` checks `VaultStatus` strictly before `SessionStatus` (AD-14) and the authenticated/expired fall-through now also includes `vaultLock`; `_GoRouterRefreshStream` generalized from one stream to `Iterable<Stream<dynamic>>` so it subscribes to both the vault and session streams — still exactly one `GoRouter`/`redirect`.
  - `lib/main.dart` — resolves `sl<VaultRepository>()`, passes it into `buildAppRouter`.
  - `ios/Runner/Info.plist` — added `NSFaceIDUsageDescription`.
  - `test/core/navigation/app_router_test.dart` — added `_FakeVaultRepository` (default `unlocked`, configurable `authenticateSucceeds`) to every call site; added 3 new cases covering "locked overrides any SessionStatus", "explicit navigation while locked bounces back to /vault", and "unlocked + authenticated at /vault routes home".
  - `test/main_test.dart` — `setUp` now swaps the real (plugin-backed) `VaultRepository` for a fake pre-`unlocked` one right after `setupCoreDependencies()`, so every pre-existing auth/session test is unaffected; added one new test exercising the cold-start-locked → `authenticate()` success → Home path end-to-end through the real `CerneApp` composition root.

  - `fvm flutter pub get` — resolves cleanly, no conflicts.

This tripped up my first draft of the unit tests (an `emittedDuring` helper that didn't account for the leading replay event) — fixed by draining that initial replay before measuring emissions caused by the action under test. Documented inline in the test file.

## Intent

**Problem:** Epic 1 left every screen reachable with no device-level access barrier; Epic 2 requires Face ID/Touch ID (PIN fallback is Story 2.2) to block all screens except the vault/login screen, on cold start, before any data is shown.

**Approach:** Add a `features/vault/` module exposing a `VaultStatus` stream that mirrors `features/auth/domain`'s `SessionStatus` pattern exactly, and extend the single existing `go_router` redirect so it composes `VaultStatus` first, then `SessionStatus` (the seam is already commented in-place). A new `/vault` route shows a minimal lock screen that auto-triggers the OS biometric prompt via `local_auth` and offers a manual retry on failure — no PIN entry UI (that's Story 2.2).

## Boundaries & Constraints

**Always:** `_redirect` checks `VaultStatus` before `SessionStatus`, never a second `GoRouter`/`redirect`. Vault makes zero network calls; `authenticate()` never produces `Failure.authInvalid` (reserved for password login). `local_auth.authenticate()` is called with `biometricOnly: true` so it never silently falls back to the OS's own device passcode screen. `VaultStatus` starts `locked` at construction (not nullable — no async warm-up needed) and only a successful `authenticate()` flips it to `unlocked`.

**Ask First:** None — remaining technical choices (lock-screen copy, retry-button wording) are decided per AGENTS.md's "decide and proceed."

**Never:** No PIN entry screen, no idle-timeout re-lock, no biometric-preference persistence — Stories 2.2/2.3/2.4. Never set `biometricOnly: false` (would let the OS's own passcode bypass Cerne's intended PIN flow).

## I/O & Edge-Case Matrix

| Scenario | Input / State | Expected Output / Behavior | Error Handling |
|----------|--------------|---------------------------|----------------|
| Cold start, biometrics succeed | `VaultStatus.locked`, app opened, OS prompt confirms | `authenticate()` emits `unlocked`; redirect falls through to existing `SessionStatus` logic (Home if authenticated) | N/A |
| Cold start, biometrics fail/cancelled/unavailable | `authenticate()` returns `false` or throws `LocalAuthException` | Status stays `locked`; lock screen shows retry button | `Left(Failure.malformedResponse(...))`, no crash |
| Any navigation while locked | `location != /vault`, `VaultStatus.locked` | redirect returns `/vault` | N/A |

</frozen-after-approval>

## Code Map

- `lib/features/auth/domain/entities/session_status.dart`, `.../repositories/session_repository.dart`, `data/repositories/session_repository_impl.dart` — exact pattern to mirror (`Stream.multi` replay-to-late-listeners, `_emit`/`isClosed` guard, `dispose:` wiring).
- `lib/core/navigation/app_router.dart:17-25` (`AppRoutePaths`), `:38-81` (`buildAppRouter`), `:94-98` (seam comment already marks this exact change), `:99-123` (`_redirect`), `:129-148` (`_GoRouterRefreshStream`, currently wraps one stream).
- `lib/main.dart:48,63-67` — `_sessionRepository = sl<SessionRepository>()` call site to mirror for vault.
- `lib/core/di/injection_container.dart:79` — `registerAuthFeature()` call site; add `registerVaultFeature()` after it.
- `lib/features/auth/auth_injection.dart` — DI registration pattern (`registerLazySingleton` + `dispose:`) to mirror.
- `lib/core/failure/failure.dart:38-39` — `Failure.malformedResponse` is the only local-failure subtype to use here.
- `pubspec.yaml:49-50` — `local_auth: ^3.0.2`, `flutter_secure_storage: ^11.2.0` already present, no change.
- `~/.pub-cache/.../local_auth-3.0.2/lib/src/local_auth.dart` — current API: `authenticate()` returns `Future<bool>`, throws `LocalAuthException` (not `PlatformException`) on error.
- `ios/Runner/Info.plist` — `NSFaceIDUsageDescription` absent, must be added.
- `test/core/navigation/app_router_test.dart` — every existing case constructs `buildAppRouter(sessionRepository: ..., ...)` directly; each call site needs a second fake `VaultRepository` (default `unlocked`) added.
- `test/main_test.dart:89-97` — `setUp` calls real `setupCoreDependencies()`; since `CerneApp` will now also resolve `sl<VaultRepository>()`, swap in a fake pre-`unlocked` one here so existing auth/session cases are unaffected.

## Tasks & Acceptance

**Execution:**
- [ ] `lib/features/vault/domain/entities/vault_status.dart` -- create `enum VaultStatus { locked, unlocked }` -- mirrors `SessionStatus`.
- [ ] `lib/features/vault/domain/repositories/vault_repository.dart` -- create `abstract class VaultRepository` (`statusStream`, non-null `currentStatus` defaulting `locked`, `authenticate()`, `dispose()`) -- mirrors `SessionRepository` (RNF09: `Either<Failure, Unit>`).
- [ ] `lib/features/vault/data/repositories/vault_repository_impl.dart` -- create `VaultRepositoryImpl(LocalAuthentication)`; `authenticate()` calls `.authenticate(localizedReason: ..., biometricOnly: true, persistAcrossBackgrounding: true)`; success emits `unlocked`+`right(unit)`; `false`/`LocalAuthException` -> `left(Failure.malformedResponse(...))`, status unchanged -- zero network, never `authInvalid`.
- [ ] `lib/features/vault/vault_injection.dart` -- create `registerVaultFeature()` -- mirrors `auth_injection.dart`.
- [ ] `lib/core/di/injection_container.dart` -- call `registerVaultFeature()` after `registerAuthFeature()`.
- [ ] `lib/core/navigation/app_router.dart` -- add `vaultLock` path; thread `vaultRepository` through `buildAppRouter`/`_redirect`; new top branch returns `vaultLock` whenever status isn't `unlocked`; extend the existing authenticated/expired `location == boot || auth` check to also include `vaultLock`; extend `_GoRouterRefreshStream` to subscribe to both streams -- composes the two gates in fixed order (AD-14).
- [ ] `lib/features/vault/presentation/screens/vault_lock_screen.dart` -- `StatefulWidget` calling `vaultRepository.authenticate()` once in `initState`, with a "Tentar novamente" retry button on failure -- no PIN UI; `DesignTokens` only.
- [ ] `lib/main.dart` -- resolve `sl<VaultRepository>()`, pass into `buildAppRouter`.
- [ ] `ios/Runner/Info.plist` -- add `NSFaceIDUsageDescription`.
- [ ] `test/features/vault/data/repositories/vault_repository_impl_test.dart` -- unit-test the I/O matrix with a mocked `LocalAuthentication`.

- [ ] `test/main_test.dart` -- swap in a fake pre-unlocked `VaultRepository` in `setUp`; add one new test: cold start stays on `/vault` until a fake `authenticate()` success routes to Home.

- Given the app is cold-started, when the vault gate evaluates, then no screen other than `/vault` is reachable until `authenticate()` succeeds.

- Given Face ID/Touch ID is available and the user opens the app, when the OS prompt succeeds, then the app routes to Home/Chat via the existing session logic, and `features/vault/domain` exposes `VaultStatus` registered once in DI.

## Design Notes

`biometricOnly: true` is the one easy-to-miss detail: `local_auth`'s default (`false`) lets the OS's own device-passcode UI satisfy `authenticate()`, which would bypass Cerne's own PIN screen (Story 2.2) entirely — `true` forces biometrics-or-fail, matching the epic's intent that PIN is Cerne's own screen, never iOS's/Android's.

`VaultStatus.currentStatus` is deliberately non-nullable (unlike `SessionStatus?`) — the vault's "locked" state is known synchronously at construction, with no async restore step, so there's no boot-loading gap to represent with `null`.

## Intent

**Problem:** Epic 1 left every screen reachable with no device-level access barrier; Epic 2 requires Face ID/Touch ID (PIN fallback is Story 2.2) to block all screens except the vault/login screen, on cold start, before any data is shown.

**Approach:** Add a `features/vault/` module exposing a `VaultStatus` stream that mirrors `features/auth/domain`'s `SessionStatus` pattern exactly, and extend the single existing `go_router` redirect so it composes `VaultStatus` first, then `SessionStatus` (the seam is already commented in-place). A new `/vault` route shows a minimal lock screen that auto-triggers the OS biometric prompt via `local_auth` and offers a manual retry on failure — no PIN entry UI (that's Story 2.2).

## Boundaries & Constraints

**Always:** `_redirect` checks `VaultStatus` before `SessionStatus`, never a second `GoRouter`/`redirect`. Vault makes zero network calls; `authenticate()` never produces `Failure.authInvalid` (reserved for password login). `local_auth.authenticate()` is called with `biometricOnly: true` so it never silently falls back to the OS's own device passcode screen. `VaultStatus` starts `locked` at construction (not nullable — no async warm-up needed) and only a successful `authenticate()` flips it to `unlocked`.

**Ask First:** None — remaining technical choices (lock-screen copy, retry-button wording) are decided per AGENTS.md's "decide and proceed."

**Never:** No PIN entry screen, no idle-timeout re-lock, no biometric-preference persistence — Stories 2.2/2.3/2.4. Never set `biometricOnly: false` (would let the OS's own passcode bypass Cerne's intended PIN flow).

## I/O & Edge-Case Matrix

| Scenario | Input / State | Expected Output / Behavior | Error Handling |
|----------|--------------|---------------------------|----------------|
| Cold start, biometrics succeed | `VaultStatus.locked`, app opened, OS prompt confirms | `authenticate()` emits `unlocked`; redirect falls through to existing `SessionStatus` logic (Home if authenticated) | N/A |
| Cold start, biometrics fail/cancelled/unavailable | `authenticate()` returns `false` or throws `LocalAuthException` | Status stays `locked`; lock screen shows retry button | `Left(Failure.malformedResponse(...))`, no crash |
| Any navigation while locked | `location != /vault`, `VaultStatus.locked` | redirect returns `/vault` | N/A |

</frozen-after-approval>

## Code Map

- `lib/features/auth/domain/entities/session_status.dart`, `.../repositories/session_repository.dart`, `data/repositories/session_repository_impl.dart` — exact pattern to mirror (`Stream.multi` replay-to-late-listeners, `_emit`/`isClosed` guard, `dispose:` wiring).
- `lib/core/navigation/app_router.dart:17-25` (`AppRoutePaths`), `:38-81` (`buildAppRouter`), `:94-98` (seam comment already marks this exact change), `:99-123` (`_redirect`), `:129-148` (`_GoRouterRefreshStream`, currently wraps one stream).
- `lib/main.dart:48,63-67` — `_sessionRepository = sl<SessionRepository>()` call site to mirror for vault.
- `lib/core/di/injection_container.dart:79` — `registerAuthFeature()` call site; add `registerVaultFeature()` after it.
- `lib/features/auth/auth_injection.dart` — DI registration pattern (`registerLazySingleton` + `dispose:`) to mirror.
- `lib/core/failure/failure.dart:38-39` — `Failure.malformedResponse` is the only local-failure subtype to use here.
- `pubspec.yaml:49-50` — `local_auth: ^3.0.2`, `flutter_secure_storage: ^11.2.0` already present, no change.
- `~/.pub-cache/.../local_auth-3.0.2/lib/src/local_auth.dart` — current API: `authenticate()` returns `Future<bool>`, throws `LocalAuthException` (not `PlatformException`) on error.
- `ios/Runner/Info.plist` — `NSFaceIDUsageDescription` absent, must be added.
- `test/core/navigation/app_router_test.dart` — every existing case constructs `buildAppRouter(sessionRepository: ..., ...)` directly; each call site needs a second fake `VaultRepository` (default `unlocked`) added.
- `test/main_test.dart:89-97` — `setUp` calls real `setupCoreDependencies()`; since `CerneApp` will now also resolve `sl<VaultRepository>()`, swap in a fake pre-`unlocked` one here so existing auth/session cases are unaffected.

## Tasks & Acceptance

**Execution:**
- [x] `lib/features/vault/domain/entities/vault_status.dart` -- create `enum VaultStatus { locked, unlocked }` -- mirrors `SessionStatus`.
- [x] `lib/features/vault/domain/repositories/vault_repository.dart` -- create `abstract class VaultRepository` (`statusStream`, non-null `currentStatus` defaulting `locked`, `authenticate()`, `dispose()`) -- mirrors `SessionRepository` (RNF09: `Either<Failure, Unit>`).
- [x] `lib/features/vault/data/repositories/vault_repository_impl.dart` -- create `VaultRepositoryImpl(LocalAuthentication)`; `authenticate()` calls `.authenticate(localizedReason: ..., biometricOnly: true, persistAcrossBackgrounding: true)`; success emits `unlocked`+`right(unit)`; `false`/`LocalAuthException` -> `left(Failure.malformedResponse(...))`, status unchanged -- zero network, never `authInvalid`.
- [x] `lib/features/vault/vault_injection.dart` -- create `registerVaultFeature()` -- mirrors `auth_injection.dart`.
- [x] `lib/core/di/injection_container.dart` -- call `registerVaultFeature()` after `registerAuthFeature()`.
- [x] `lib/core/navigation/app_router.dart` -- add `vaultLock` path; thread `vaultRepository` through `buildAppRouter`/`_redirect`; new top branch returns `vaultLock` whenever status isn't `unlocked`; extend the existing authenticated/expired `location == boot || auth` check to also include `vaultLock`; extend `_GoRouterRefreshStream` to subscribe to both streams -- composes the two gates in fixed order (AD-14).
- [x] `lib/features/vault/presentation/screens/vault_lock_screen.dart` -- `StatefulWidget` calling `vaultRepository.authenticate()` once in `initState`, with a "Tentar novamente" retry button on failure -- no PIN UI; `DesignTokens` only.
- [x] `lib/main.dart` -- resolve `sl<VaultRepository>()`, pass into `buildAppRouter`.
- [x] `ios/Runner/Info.plist` -- add `NSFaceIDUsageDescription`.
- [x] `test/features/vault/data/repositories/vault_repository_impl_test.dart` -- unit-test the I/O matrix with a mocked `LocalAuthentication`.
- [x] `test/core/navigation/app_router_test.dart` -- add a fake `VaultRepository` (default `unlocked`) to every existing call site; add cases: locked overrides any `SessionStatus`; unlocked + authenticated at `/vault` routes home.
- [x] `test/main_test.dart` -- swap in a fake pre-unlocked `VaultRepository` in `setUp`; add one new test: cold start stays on `/vault` until a fake `authenticate()` success routes to Home.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- Given the app is cold-started, when the vault gate evaluates, then no screen other than `/vault` is reachable until `authenticate()` succeeds.
- Given the redirect evaluates on any navigation attempt, then it composes exactly two gates in fixed order (`VaultStatus` then `SessionStatus`) and neither ever makes a network call.
- Given Face ID/Touch ID is available and the user opens the app, when the OS prompt succeeds, then the app routes to Home/Chat via the existing session logic, and `features/vault/domain` exposes `VaultStatus` registered once in DI.

## Design Notes

`biometricOnly: true` is the one easy-to-miss detail: `local_auth`'s default (`false`) lets the OS's own device-passcode UI satisfy `authenticate()`, which would bypass Cerne's own PIN screen (Story 2.2) entirely — `true` forces biometrics-or-fail, matching the epic's intent that PIN is Cerne's own screen, never iOS's/Android's.

`VaultStatus.currentStatus` is deliberately non-nullable (unlike `SessionStatus?`) — the vault's "locked" state is known synchronously at construction, with no async restore step, so there's no boot-loading gap to represent with `null`.

## Verification

**Commands:**
- `fvm flutter analyze` -- expected: zero issues.
- `fvm flutter test` -- expected: all pass, including new vault tests.

**Manual checks (if no CLI):**
- No device/simulator exists yet (AGENTS.md) — the real OS biometric prompt itself is unverifiable until one does; this is a known, pre-existing gap, not introduced by this story.

1	# Verification Gap Review
2	
3	**Goal:** Find changed behavior that could break without reliable verification catching it. Ask one question — "if the behavior this change is supposed to produce broke where it's actually used, would verification fail?" Do not hunt for correctness bugs, but report genuine problems you notice while tracing verification.
4	
5	The main verification gap shapes are:
6	
7	1. **Regression gap:** the changed code regresses where it's used, and no test covering that use would fail.
8	2. **Missing-adoption gap:** a place that should now use the new behavior doesn't; it handles the same case its own way, or not at all, and no test would flag the omission.
9	3. **Broken-verification gap:** a test appears to cover the changed behavior, but would not actually protect it because it is skipped, flaky, not run in the normal verification path, or too weak to observe the regression.
10	
11	## Evidence Rules
12	
13	- Read a test before claiming what it covers, runs, asserts, or misses.
14	- Before claiming no test exists, search the whole repo by the symbol under test and by import references; expected file locations are not enough.
15	- Never assert what you did not verify. If a finding cannot be grounded, drop it.
16	- In a finding, say what you actually checked — "none of the tests I read cover this" — and show how far you looked. Say a test doesn't exist anywhere only when the symbol/import-reference search actually shows that.
17	- Do not assign severity, confidence, priority, or ranking.
18	
19	## Review Sequence
20	
21	### Step 1: Screen for behavioral change
22	
23	Screen each part of the change separately. If a part is non-behavioral, skip it. Call a part non-behavioral only when the changed code does not alter return values, thrown errors, caller-visible side effects, or observable state (including iteration order and emitted messages). Once a part meets that test, move on; do not inspect callers or tests for extra confirmation.
24	
25	Common non-behavioral examples: formatting, comments, whitespace; pure renames; trivial getters/setters and pass-throughs; type-only or compiler-enforced changes with no runtime effect; etc.
26	
27	Only outcomes produced by deterministic code are worth automatically testing; tests are useless on static source text and brittle on LLM output. Skip those parts.
28	
29	If every part is skipped, output the clean result (see Output Format).
30	
31	### Step 2: Find the behavior that changed
32	
33	Identify what behavior changed compared to the previous version: output, side effect, branch, error path, schema/event shape, config default, validation/authorization rule, external contract, etc. If the change affects more than one behavior, handle each separately.
34	
35	Treat broad-impact changes as behavioral even when no single changed line looks important: dependency, toolchain, build/config, data-file, etc.
36	
37	### Step 3: Trace where that behavior is used
38	
39	Trace the changed behavior to the places that observe it. Start with direct callers and registered entry points (routes, commands, DI), contract consumers (schemas, events, APIs, database readers), and reverse-dependency info if already available.
40	
41	Follow a path only while the changed behavior is reachable and unverified. Stop when a test at that boundary would fail, the consumer does not observe the changed behavior, or the next hop is guesswork (dynamic dispatch, reflection, outside-repo consumers, etc.). Prefer the nearest observable boundary, often one to three hops away, especially across contract, integration, or service edges. If there are more than five similar consumers, group obvious repeats and check representative paths; expand only when a consumer observes the behavior differently.
42

# Verification Gap Review

**Goal:** Find changed behavior that could break without reliable verification catching it. Ask one question — "if the behavior this change is supposed to produce broke where it's actually used, would verification fail?" Do not hunt for correctness bugs, but report genuine problems you notice while tracing verification.

The main verification gap shapes are:

1. **Regression gap:** the changed code regresses where it's used, and no test covering that use would fail.
2. **Missing-adoption gap:** a place that should now use the new behavior doesn't; it handles the same case its own way, or not at all, and no test would flag the omission.
3. **Broken-verification gap:** a test appears to cover the changed behavior, but would not actually protect it because it is skipped, flaky, not run in the normal verification path, or too weak to observe the regression.

## Evidence Rules

- Read a test before claiming what it covers, runs, asserts, or misses.
- Before claiming no test exists, search the whole repo by the symbol under test and by import references; expected file locations are not enough.
- Never assert what you did not verify. If a finding cannot be grounded, drop it.
- In a finding, say what you actually checked — "none of the tests I read cover this" — and show how far you looked. Say a test doesn't exist anywhere only when the symbol/import-reference search actually shows that.
- Do not assign severity, confidence, priority, or ranking.

## Review Sequence

### Step 1: Screen for behavioral change

Screen each part of the change separately. If a part is non-behavioral, skip it. Call a part non-behavioral only when the changed code does not alter return values, thrown errors, caller-visible side effects, or observable state (including iteration order and emitted messages). Once a part meets that test, move on; do not inspect callers or tests for extra confirmation.

Common non-behavioral examples: formatting, comments, whitespace; pure renames; trivial getters/setters and pass-throughs; type-only or compiler-enforced changes with no runtime effect; etc.

Only outcomes produced by deterministic code are worth automatically testing; tests are useless on static source text and brittle on LLM output. Skip those parts.

If every part is skipped, output the clean result (see Output Format).

### Step 2: Find the behavior that changed

Identify what behavior changed compared to the previous version: output, side effect, branch, error path, schema/event shape, config default, validation/authorization rule, external contract, etc. If the change affects more than one behavior, handle each separately.

Treat broad-impact changes as behavioral even when no single changed line looks important: dependency, toolchain, build/config, data-file, etc.

### Step 3: Trace where that behavior is used

Trace the changed behavior to the places that observe it. Start with direct callers and registered entry points (routes, commands, DI), contract consumers (schemas, events, APIs, database readers), and reverse-dependency info if already available.

Follow a path only while the changed behavior is reachable and unverified. Stop when a test at that boundary would fail, the consumer does not observe the changed behavior, or the next hop is guesswork (dynamic dispatch, reflection, outside-repo consumers, etc.). Prefer the nearest observable boundary, often one to three hops away, especially across contract, integration, or service edges. If there are more than five similar consumers, group obvious repeats and check representative paths; expand only when a consumer observes the behavior differently.

### Step 4: Qualify the consumer, then check its test

For each consumer, name the smallest realistic regression this consumer would observe: invert the branch, drop the default, omit the field, return the old error code, skip the integration call, etc. This is the Demonstration. If no such regression exists, drop the path; untested downstream code is not a finding.

A `Missing-adoption gap` qualifies not by the adoption failure alone but by a supersession signal: the change gives clear evidence the new behavior is meant to replace the local one — PR intent, naming or docs, a replaced sibling site, deleted duplicate logic, or a test defining the new rule — and the local site shares the same observable contract. Without a supersession signal and a shared observable contract, it is a refactor suggestion, not a verification-gap finding. Once both hold, check whether any test for that site would flag the non-adoption; missing coverage of the non-adoption is the gap itself, not a disqualifier.

Find and read the relevant test. Ask whether the Demonstration would make an assertion fail.

- If yes, the behavior is verified. No finding.
- For a regression-style Demonstration: if no test runs the path, the test is skipped/flaky/not run normally, or the test runs the code without checking the changed result, report a `Regression gap` or `Broken-verification gap`.
- For a qualifying Missing-adoption case: if none of the site tests you found assert it adopts the new behavior, report a `Missing-adoption gap`.

A test counts only if it runs normally and an assertion observes the changed output, branch, or contract. These do not count: no execution; source-text assertions that match a file's wording instead of running it; success/no-throw/snapshot-only checks; mock/log-call checks; human-only checks; tests that mock away the integration; e2e tests that pass through without checking the changed output; stale assertions or fixtures.

For example, `expect(x ?? DEFAULT).toBe(DEFAULT)` passes when `x` is missing.

Common patterns:

- **Caller-path gap** — helper test covers the branch, but caller values skip it.
- **Contract drift** — payload/schema/event changes must be verified at the consumer.
- **Migration compatibility** — tests only create new-format rows or fresh schemas.
- **Phantom exception** — handled partial-failure path has no test.
- **Missing-adoption gap** — sibling site should use the new rule/helper and does not.
- **Removed verification** — deleted test or weakened assertion leaves behavior unpinned; removing a source-text assertion is not this, since it never counted.

### Step 5: Confirm each finding is real

Before writing a finding, re-open the specific tests or search results the finding relies on. Verify the Demonstration would not make any test you checked fail, or that the absence claim is backed by the symbol/import-reference search. Do not claim more than you verified; drop any finding you cannot ground.

Explain why the test misses the bug using what the test sets up and checks.

Do not report: compiler/type-checker-enforced cases; behavior already verified by an integration, contract, or e2e test; implementation-detail or mock-only tests; low coverage or a missing test file by itself; legacy untested code the change did not affect.

Report genuine problems you noticed while tracing verification, even if they are not verification gaps. Put them under `Other findings` in the output. This permits reporting what you already reached, not extra hunting.

## OUTPUT FORMAT

Emit each verification-gap finding as one block. No general advice, no severity or confidence.

```markdown
### <one-line title naming the gap>

- **Changed surface:** the exact behavior or contract that changed — `file:line`.
- **Impacted consumer or site:** named concretely with `file:line` (e.g. "the `createInvoice` mutation used by the billing dashboard at `billing/dashboard.ts:88`," not "callers of this function").
- **Existing test evidence:**
  - `Regression gap`: what the relevant test actually asserts, with `file:line`; or, if none, the symbol/import-reference searches run and their result.
  - `Missing-adoption gap`: tests for the impacted site, and whether any assert it adopts the new behavior.
  - `Broken-verification gap`: the apparent test or verification path, and why it does not count.
- **Missing verification:** the precise assertion or check that's absent.
- **Demonstration:**
  - `Regression gap` / `Broken-verification gap`: the concrete regression that would ship undetected, and why the tests you checked would not fail.
  - `Missing-adoption gap`: the case the site mishandles by not adopting the new behavior, and that none of the tests you read assert adoption.
- **Consequence:** the concrete thing that ships wrong — a regression the checked evidence would not catch, or a site that should use the new behavior and doesn't.
- **Suggested test shape:** (optional) the kind of test that would close the gap, fit to the repo's own way of verifying — don't impose a generic test pyramid.
```

If you noticed genuine non-gap problems while tracing verification, append:

```markdown
## Other findings

- <description only; no severity, confidence, priority, or ranking>
```

When you find no verification gaps and no other findings, output exactly this single line, not an empty response:

`No verification gaps found.`

## CONTENT SOURCE

Review the content supplied under "Review content:" in the message that launched you. If none is supplied, stop with exactly: `No verification gaps found.`

Verification confirms: this project has no `android/` directory at all (iOS-only, consistent with AGENTS.md), and `LocalAuthException` + the `authenticate()` signature the implementation used are exactly what `package:local_auth/local_auth.dart` 3.0.2 exports — both already double-checked against source during planning, and `flutter analyze`/`flutter test` passing is independent confirmation. So several Blind Hunter claims are factually wrong.

**Classification of all findings:**

**Reject (incorrect or already covered by the approved spec's explicit scope):**
- "`authenticate()` signature won't compile," "`LocalAuthException` not exported," "pubspec.yaml missing `local_auth`" — all three are factually false; I verified the real package source directly and `flutter analyze`/`test` pass clean.
- "No Android setup" — project has no `android/` directory; iOS-only.
- "No re-lock after unlock," "no PIN fallback," "no logout escape hatch," "`malformedResponse` overloaded," "no `canCheckBiometrics` precheck" — all explicitly out of scope per the frozen spec's **Never** section (Stories 2.2/2.3/2.4's job) or a deliberate, documented Code Map decision.
- "Files not shown in diff" — an artifact of how I trimmed that subagent's prompt, not a real gap; I verified those files directly myself.
- ExpiryOverlayHost-over-locked-vault race, `_GoRouterRefreshStream` constructor throw mid-loop, `_vaultRepository.dispose()` never called from widget teardown — all unreachable in the current call graph or mirror a pre-existing, unchanged pattern (`_sessionRepository` isn't disposed from widget teardown either).

**Patch (real, trivially fixable, applying now):**
1. **Verification gap (well-evidenced):** `registerVaultFeature()`'s DI wiring is never force-resolved by any test — `bootstrap_integration_test.dart` proves the analogous auth chain this same way but was never extended to vault, so a broken registration would only surface at real app launch.
2. The fakes' `authenticateSucceeds` field is declared but never set `true` anywhere, and `VaultLockScreen`'s "Tentar novamente" button is never actually tapped in a widget test — the retry path is unverified end-to-end.
3. `VaultLockScreen` has no `Semantics`/live-region announcement for the lock→retry state change, despite the loaded epic context explicitly requiring screen-reader announcement of failure-state transitions.

Re-engaging the implementation subagent with these three patches.

input.prompt:
SendMessage to: a280d6b8d96889734

Code review of your spec-2-1 (biometric vault gate) implementation found three real, trivially-fixable gaps. Apply these three patches, then re-run verification:

1. **DI wiring never force-resolved in a test.** `test/core/di/bootstrap_integration_test.dart` already proves the analogous auth DI chain by forcing resolution right after `setupCoreDependencies()` (its existing test asserts `sl.isRegistered<AuthRepository>()`, `sl.isRegistered<AuthCubit>()`, and `expect(() => sl<AuthCubit>(), returnsNormally)`). The new `registerVaultFeature()` wiring was never given the same treatment — no test anywhere force-resolves `sl<VaultRepository>()` against its real registration before something swaps or resets it (confirmed: `test/main_test.dart`'s `setUp` unregisters/swaps `VaultRepository` for a fake immediately after `setupCoreDependencies()`, before any resolution; `app_router_test.dart` never calls `setupCoreDependencies()` at all; the new `vault_repository_impl_test.dart` constructs `VaultRepositoryImpl` directly, bypassing `sl`). A broken registration (bad factory, missing `LocalAuthentication` dependency, broken `dispose:`) would only surface at real app launch, which this project has no device/CI to catch. Fix: in `test/core/di/bootstrap_integration_test.dart`, add assertions mirroring the existing auth ones — `expect(sl.isRegistered<VaultRepository>(), isTrue);` and `expect(() => sl<VaultRepository>(), returnsNormally);` — in the same test block that already force-resolves the auth chain (or a new adjacent test). This is safe: resolving `VaultRepository` only constructs `VaultRepositoryImpl(localAuthentication: sl<LocalAuthentication>())`, which just stores the `LocalAuthentication()` instance — it never calls any of its methods, so no platform-channel mock is needed (same reasoning that already applies to `AuthCubit`'s forced resolution in that file).

2. **Retry path never exercised end-to-end.** In both `test/core/navigation/app_router_test.dart` and `test/main_test.dart`, the `_FakeVaultRepository.authenticateSucceeds` field is declared and checked in `authenticate()` but never set to `true` anywhere — every test that unlocks the vault does so via `setStatus(VaultStatus.unlocked)` directly, never by actually tapping `VaultLockScreen`'s "Tentar novamente" button. Add one widget test (in `test/main_test.dart`'s existing `group('AD-14 — VaultStatus gate composed ahead of SessionStatus (spec-2-1)', ...)` is a natural home, or `vault_lock_screen_test.dart` if you prefer a dedicated presentation-layer test file under `test/features/vault/presentation/screens/`) that: mounts `VaultLockScreen` (or `CerneApp` with vault locked) with a fake `VaultRepository` whose `authenticateSucceeds` starts `false`; confirms the retry button is visible after the initial auto-attempt fails; flips `authenticateSucceeds = true`; taps "Tentar novamente"; and confirms the vault unlocks (e.g. the screen navigates away, or `currentStatus` becomes `unlocked`). This should use the field for real and prove the button's `onPressed: _attemptAuthenticate` wiring actually re-invokes `authenticate()` and reacts to success.

3. **No screen-reader announcement of the lock/retry state change.** `lib/features/vault/presentation/screens/vault_lock_screen.dart` has no `Semantics` wrapping for its status text — the loaded epic-2-context.md's UX & Interaction Patterns explicitly requires "Screen-reader labels must announce the failure transition (state changes, not just static state)," same accessibility floor already applied elsewhere in this epic. Fix: wrap the status `Column` (or at minimum the headline/body `Text` pair) in a `Semantics(liveRegion: true, ...)` so VoiceOver announces the transition from "autenticando" to the retry state, rather than staying silent. Keep it minimal — no new strings beyond what's already there, just the `liveRegion` wiring.

After applying all three, re-run `fvm flutter analyze` (expect zero issues) and `fvm flutter test` (expect all tests, including the new retry-path test, to pass). Report back what you changed and the verification output.

## Suggested Review Order

**Redirect composition (AD-14)**

- Entry point: the vault gate is checked strictly before `SessionStatus`, returning early whenever not `unlocked`.
  [`app_router.dart:125`](../../lib/core/navigation/app_router.dart#L125)

- `vaultLock` is folded into the existing boot/auth fall-through so unlocking while still at `/vault` reaches Home.
  [`app_router.dart:149`](../../lib/core/navigation/app_router.dart#L149)

- `buildAppRouter` now requires both repositories as parameters, never reaching into `sl` itself.
  [`app_router.dart:45`](../../lib/core/navigation/app_router.dart#L45)

- New `/vault` route constant, added alongside Story 1.6's original set.
  [`app_router.dart:25`](../../lib/core/navigation/app_router.dart#L25)

**VaultRepository contract and implementation**

- The domain contract: non-nullable `currentStatus` (no boot-loading gap, unlike `SessionStatus?`), `Either<Failure, Unit>` return (RNF09).
  [`vault_repository.dart:14`](../../lib/features/vault/domain/repositories/vault_repository.dart#L14)

- `biometricOnly: true` — the one easy-to-miss detail preventing the OS's own passcode screen from silently satisfying this call.
  [`vault_repository_impl.dart:73`](../../lib/features/vault/data/repositories/vault_repository_impl.dart#L73)

- `LocalAuthException` maps to `Failure.malformedResponse`, never `authInvalid` — zero network calls anywhere in this class.
